phase-summary.outcome: Resolved the docs-site Vercel build blockers by removing recursive workspace install behavior from lifecycle scripts and splitting a runtime-only engine entrypoint for Next server imports. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now completes without re-entering docs-site postinstall, and `pnpm --dir docs-site run build:vercel-parity` completes successfully.

file.description: Removed KAPLAY bootstrap from `postinstall` so install stays focused on dependency setup and MDX generation.
Stopped nested `pnpm install` calls; the script now only builds/copies the optional iframe asset.
Added a runtime-only export surface for server/shared imports that must not pull in React hooks.
Kept the root package API client-friendly by re-exporting runtime symbols plus `DungeonBreakGame`.
Published the new `./runtime` subpath and built it as part of the engine package.
Server-side engine import moved to the runtime-only subpath.
Shared MCP parsing logic now imports action metadata from the runtime-only entrypoint.
Server-rendered play report generation now avoids the client component export surface.
Shared space explorer helpers now depend on the runtime-only engine entrypoint.
Server route type imports now align with the runtime-only engine subpath.

decision.summary: Workspace lifecycle scripts must not trigger nested package-manager installs.
decision.impact: Prevents recursive install loops on Vercel and keeps local CI parity runs predictable.

decision.summary: Server and shared Next modules should import engine runtime symbols from `@dungeonbreak/engine/runtime` instead of the root package entry.
decision.impact: Preserves the root client-friendly API while keeping Next server routes free of React hook imports.

tests.test: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (passed; docs-site postinstall no longer re-enters KAPLAY/bootstrap install)

next.action: Rerun any previously blocked production-style verification flows, especially phase 50 E2E checks and the next Vercel deployment using Node 20.x.

suggestion.gap: Phase 52 requirements do not explicitly call out non-recursive deploy hooks or separate server-safe package entrypoints for Next runtime consumers.
suggestion.proposal: Add a CI/CD requirement stating that docs-site deploy/install hooks must avoid nested workspace installs and that shared engine packages expose a server-safe runtime entry for non-client code.
